subject: Proposal: variability corridor + stability-credit draft for pricing schedule
messages:

Subject: Proposal: variability corridor + stability-credit draft for pricing schedule

James — attaching a clean and a lightly marked version of the pricing appendix (v3) with two things we want to resolve before legal final: the variability corridor (how much the commit can swing without trigger) and the stability-credit mechanics (temporary credit if usage drops below commit during onboarding).

High level ask: can you review the attached markup and confirm Novus’s tolerance for a corridor of +/- 10% versus +/- 5%?

Key points we flagged in the markup: 
- Corridor: proposes a +/-10% swing before true-up; if usage drops beyond that, standard true‑up applies at the next billing quarter.
- Stability credit: a one‑time onboarding credit limited to 6 months and capped at 10% of the first quarter’s invoice, subject to a clawback if net usage stays below commit after month 9.
- Downside protection: proposed floor language that prevents retroactive credits beyond 6 months unless there is documented outage or regional capacity failure.

Attachments: Novus_Pricing_Appendix_v3.pdf (clean), KP_markup_variability_stability.docx (comments).

Proposed next steps: if you’re okay with +/-10% corridor, we’ll push the redline to legal and send a single tracked document back for countersign. If you prefer +/-5%, please indicate and we’ll propose the offsetting operational concession (longer advance notice on volume changes or a shorter stability credit window).

Thanks —

Kimberly — thanks for the note and the attachments. We reviewed the marked appendix with finance and have two quick questions: 

1) Is the +/-10% corridor applied month-over-month or measured at quarter level? Our preference is quarter-level smoothing.
2) For the stability credit, instead of a blunt 6-month window, can we propose an earned credit that vests 25% at month 2, 50% at month 4, and 100% at month 6 (so there’s automatic tapering)?

I’m looping in contracts as requested. If we can agree the corridor will be quarter-measured and the stability credit uses a vesting approach, Novus is much more comfortable. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call this week to align.

—James

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-19T14:20:00Z
Subject: RE: Proposal: variability corridor + stability-credit draft for pricing schedule

Kimberly / Marissa — I read James’s note. High-level legal/ops thoughts below and a suggested redline excerpt we can push to Novus if they accept quarter-level measurement and a vesting-style credit.

Quick clarifications: 
- Corridor measurement: we should explicitly state "measured on a rolling calendar quarter basis" to avoid month-end gaming.
- Credit vesting: acceptable, but add a clawback that is limited in scope (only applies to credits earned in first 6 months and only if average usage in months 7–12 remains below 90% of committed volume).
- Cap on exposure: limit total stability-credit exposure to 10% of estimated first-quarter ARR or $75k, whichever is lower.

Suggested redline language (to paste into the appendix):
"Variability Corridor and Stability Credit. The parties agree that for the purposes of true‑up and invoice adjustments, the Variability Corridor shall be measured on a rolling calendar quarter basis. If Customer usage remains within the Variability Corridor (plus/minus ten percent (10%)) for the applicable rolling calendar quarter, no true‑up shall be applied for that quarter.

During the initial onboarding period (the first six (6) months following the Effective Date), Customer may be eligible to receive a Stability Credit that vests according to the following schedule: twenty‑five percent (25%) at the end of month two (2), fifty percent (50%) at the end of month four (4), and one hundred percent (100%) at the end of month six (6), subject to the Cap described below. Any Stability Credit paid or applied shall be subject to a clawback if Customer’s average monthly usage over months seven (7) through twelve (12) is less than ninety percent (90%) of the Customer’s committed volume, in which case Customer shall repay the pro‑rata portion of the Stability Credit within thirty (30) days of notice.

The total Stability Credit exposure shall be capped at the lesser of (a) ten percent (10%) of Customer’s estimated first‑quarter Annual Recurring Revenue, or (b) seventy‑five thousand U.S. dollars (US$75,000). Clawback rights shall not apply in the event of documented service interruption attributable to Redwood’s failure to provide capacity in Customer’s agreed region.

This language is intentionally tight to limit retrospective liabilities while giving Novus a predictable ramp support mechanism"

I attached pricing_redline_karthik.docx with the text. If we get sign-off from Kimberly, I’ll ask Legal to run the final style pass and then we can send a single tracked PDF.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Commercial Contracts, Redwood Inference

James — appreciate the quick turn. We agree to your quarter-level measurement ask and Karthik’s vesting + clawback language. Next steps: 

1) Please confirm Novus is comfortable with the +/-10% corridor measured at the rolling calendar quarter level (we will include the exact formula in the appendix).
2) Confirm the cap approach above (lesser of 10% of estimated first-quarter ARR or $75k). If you want a straight dollar cap instead, let us know the number you prefer.
3) If Novus signs off on 1 and 2, we’ll have Legal apply final style and send a single tracked PDF for countersign. We can target DocuSign by EOD Friday if approved.

If helpful I can schedule a 30-minute sync with James + Novus contracts + Karthik this Thursday 11am PT to walk through the redline and get a verbal yes. Otherwise please reply with explicit confirmation on the two points above.

Thanks —
Kim
